title: Crime — Computer & Funds Transfer Fraud (Policy C)

clauses.heading: Insuring Agreement — Computer & Funds Transfer Fraud
clauses.text: We will pay for loss of Money resulting directly from Computer Fraud, including loss resulting from the Insured's transfer of Money in reliance on a Fraudulent Instruction.

clauses.heading: Definitions — Computer Fraud
clauses.text: "Computer Fraud" means the unlawful taking of Money through unauthorized entry into the Insured's Computer System, where the resulting transfer is initiated without the knowledge or consent of any Employee.

clauses.heading: Definitions — Fraudulent Instruction
clauses.text: "Fraudulent Instruction" means an electronic instruction that constitutes Computer Fraud and on which an Employee relies in initiating the transfer of Money.

check.question: Can the Fraudulent Instruction coverage the insuring clause names ever pay?

plain_english_why: The insuring clause advertises coverage for transfers made in reliance on a Fraudulent Instruction — the classic social-engineering loss, where a deceived Employee initiates the payment. But D2 requires every Fraudulent Instruction to constitute Computer Fraud, and D1 requires Computer Fraud to involve a transfer initiated without the knowledge or consent of any Employee. A transfer an Employee initiates in reliance on an instruction cannot also be a transfer no Employee initiated. The social-engineering coverage G1 names cannot pay any claim: the definitions gut the grant.
